title: Diabetes and surgery: medication plan and variable-rate insulin

related.why: The other common pre-assessment medication plan: anticoagulants

brief.scenario: Mrs Janet Price, 62, has type 2 diabetes and is listed for an elective laparoscopic right hemicolectomy on a morning list. She takes Humalog Mix 25 twice daily, metformin 1 g twice daily and dapagliflozin 10 mg daily. Her HbA1c is 68 mmol/mol.
brief.task: Answer the examiner's questions on her perioperative diabetes management.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Each drug has its own rule; then glucose control while she can't eat.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Running insulin without a glucose-and-saline substrate, or forgetting the SGLT2 inhibitor.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "Her HbA1c is below 69, so surgery can go ahead."

grid.label: Pre-op risk and HbA1c
grid.fail: Doesn't use the HbA1c, or delays surgery for an HbA1c of 68.
grid.pass: HbA1c 68 is below 69 mmol/mol, so proceed; above 69, refer to the diabetes specialist team.
grid.high: Names the risks: infection, poor healing, hypoglycaemia, DKA; and flags her for the first slot on the list.

grid.label: Insulin and metformin
grid.fail: Omits all insulin on the day, or gives the full morning dose.
grid.pass: Premixed insulin: usual doses the day before; halve the morning dose on the day; glucose on admission. Metformin twice daily: take as normal.
grid.high: Adds that metformin is omitted on the day and for 48 hours if contrast is given and eGFR is under 60.

grid.label: SGLT2 inhibitor (safety-critical)
grid.fail: Continues dapagliflozin, or doesn't mention it.
grid.pass: Omit dapagliflozin the day before and the day of surgery: risk of euglycaemic DKA.
grid.high: Restarts only when ketones are normal and she is eating normally; checks blood ketones if unwell, whatever the glucose.

grid.label: Need for VRIII
grid.fail: Plans subcutaneous insulin only through several days of fasting.
grid.pass: VRIII because she is insulin-treated and will miss more than one meal.
grid.high: Continues a long-acting analogue at 80% of the usual dose when a patient on basal insulin starts VRIII.

grid.label: VRIII prescription (safety-critical)
grid.fail: Gives insulin without substrate, or 10% glucose at 100 ml/h.
grid.pass: 50 units soluble insulin in 49.5 ml 0.9% saline (1 unit/ml); 0.45% saline with 5% glucose and potassium alongside, at maintenance rate.
grid.high: Sets maintenance at 25-30 ml/kg/day and states the substrate rate isn't changed without senior advice.

grid.label: Targets and monitoring
grid.fail: Doesn't know the target, or checks glucose 4-hourly.
grid.pass: Hourly capillary glucose; target 6-10 mmol/l, up to 12 acceptable. Hypoglycaemia below 4.
grid.high: Daily electrolytes for potassium and sodium; treats hypoglycaemia and restarts insulin within 20 minutes.

grid.label: Stopping VRIII
grid.fail: Stops the VRIII before any subcutaneous insulin is given.
grid.pass: When eating and drinking: usual insulin with a meal, then stop VRIII at least 30 minutes later.
grid.high: Involves the diabetes inpatient team; reduces premixed dose if she eats only half a meal.

failures.move: Running insulin without a glucose-and-saline substrate.
failures.consequence: Safety-critical: hypoglycaemia and hyponatraemia; 10% glucose alone gives no sodium.
Safety-critical: euglycaemic DKA, missed because the glucose looks normal.

failures.move: Stopping the VRIII before subcutaneous insulin is given.
failures.consequence: An insulin gap: rebound hyperglycaemia and ketosis.

failures.move: Omitting all insulin on the morning of surgery.

recovery.line: Insulin always runs with a glucose-and-saline substrate, and potassium; I'd follow the CPOC prescription.

recovery.when: Asked about a drug you don't know
recovery.line: I'd check the CPOC table for that drug and ask the diabetes team.

knowledge.fact: HbA1c above 69 mmol/mol (8.5%): refer to the diabetes specialist team before elective surgery.
SGLT2 inhibitors: omit the day before and the day of surgery; restart when ketones are normal and eating.
Twice-daily premixed insulin: no change the day before; halve the morning dose on the day.
VRIII if insulin-treated and more than one missed meal: 50 units soluble insulin in 49.5 ml 0.9% saline.
Substrate: 0.45% saline with 5% glucose and 0.15% or 0.3% potassium chloride at maintenance rate.
Glucose target 6-10 mmol/l (up to 12 acceptable); hourly on VRIII.

recall.think: Hypoglycaemia, DKA (including euglycaemic), hyperglycaemia and infection.
recall.say: "She needs a VRIII with a glucose-saline substrate."
do: Omit SGLT2 inhibitor day before and day of

numbers.meaning: HbA1c above this: diabetes team first

recall.trap: A normal glucose does not exclude DKA on an SGLT2 inhibitor.
recall.finish: Usual insulin with a meal; stop VRIII 30 minutes later.

sources.name: Centre for Perioperative Care. Guideline for perioperative care for people with diabetes mellitus undergoing elective and emergency surgery
sources.version: Version 3.0, 4 October 2023 (first published March 2021; version 2.0 December 2022)
sources.supports: Refer to the diabetes specialist team if HbA1c above 69 mmol/mol (8.5%); medication table: premixed twice-daily insulin no change the day before, halve the morning dose on the day and check glucose on admission, half dose with a half meal; metformin take as normal (omit on the day and for 48 hours if contrast and eGFR under 60); SGLT2 inhibitors omitted the day before and the day of surgery, restarted once ketones normal and eating; VRIII if insulin-treated with more than one missed meal; 50 units soluble human insulin in 49.5 ml 0.9% sodium chloride; substrate 5% dextrose in 0.45% saline with 0.15% or 0.3% KCl at maintenance rate, not altered without senior advice; long-acting analogues continued at 80%; hourly CBG, target 6-10 mmol/l (up to 12 acceptable); hypoglycaemia below 4 mmol/l, restart insulin within 20 minutes; subcutaneous insulin at least 30 minutes before stopping VRIII; first on the list

sources.name: NICE CG174: Intravenous fluid therapy in adults in hospital
sources.supports: Routine maintenance 25-30 ml/kg/day of water with about 1 mmol/kg/day of sodium, potassium and chloride

Asks about her usual glucose control
Asks about glucose on the ward on day 1

push.question: Can she go ahead with this HbA1c?
What will you do with each of her medicines?
push.expect: Halve morning premixed insulin; metformin as normal; omit dapagliflozin day before and day of.

push.question: Does she need a VRIII?
push.expect: Yes: insulin-treated, more than one missed meal.

push.question: Write the VRIII prescription.
push.expect: 50 units in 49.5 ml 0.9% saline; 0.45% saline with 5% glucose and KCl at maintenance rate.

push.question: What glucose target?
push.expect: 6-10 mmol/l, up to 12 acceptable; hourly checks.

curveballs.prompt: The ward suggests 10% glucose at 100 ml/h as the substrate.
curveballs.safeAnswer: No: use 0.45% saline with 5% glucose and potassium at her maintenance rate, per CPOC.

curveballs.prompt: Day 2: glucose 8, she feels sick and breathless.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Check blood ketones and a gas for euglycaemic DKA; escalate and involve the diabetes team.
Refer to the diabetes specialist team to optimise before surgery, weighing the urgency of the operation with the surgical team.

curveballs.prompt: Capillary glucose on the VRIII is 3.2 mmol/l.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Stop the insulin, treat the hypoglycaemia, recheck, and restart insulin within 20 minutes once glucose recovers.
